title: Dietary fiber increases beneficial gut bacteria
statement: A high-fiber diet selectively promotes the growth of beneficial gut bacteria that produce short-chain fatty acids.
mechanism: Dietary fiber serves as a prebiotic substrate fermented by commensal bacteria such as Faecalibacterium and Bifidobacterium, leading to increased SCFA production and reduced gut permeability.
predictions: Higher fiber intake increases Faecalibacterium abundance
